rules.R1: A weekday pattern ("todos los lunes de julio") gives one single-day option per date.
rules.R2: A weekend gives one range option, Saturday to Sunday. "Fin de semana" or "weekend" naming the kind of plan beside its own dates is not a date: only those dates are read ("weekend trip from Friday 17 to Sunday 19 July" = 17→19 July; owner, 2026-11-12). "Sábado y domingo" said beside weekends already named says which days of them are meant and never adds this weekend: "todos los fines de semana de julio, sábado y domingo, por la mañana" = each Saturday and Sunday of July as a single day (owner, 2026-11-12). "El fin de semana del 25 y 26 de julio" (Catalan "el cap de setmana de l'11 i 12 de juliol", English "the weekend of the 25th and 26th of July") is that weekend, one range, never this weekend nor a second Sunday (owner, 2026-11-12). "Todo el fin de semana", "tot el cap de setmana", "the whole weekend" said right after a weekend already named is that weekend again, never a second option: "el cap de setmana del 18 i 19 de juliol, quedem tot el cap de setmana" = 18→19 July; alone it is this weekend (owner, 2026-11-13). Day numbers set after a named weekend and listed with "y" are its days, said again: "el primer finde de agosto, el 1 y el 2" = 1→2 August only; ones that are not its days give no option and the *does not fit* notice ("el primer finde de agosto, el 8 y el 9"; owner, 2026-11-13).
rules.R3: A pattern over the current month takes the dates left in it, today included ("todos los lunes de junio" on 15 June: 15, 22, 29).
rules.R4: A day and month (or a month) already past this year means next year; a day and month that passed 30 days ago or less gives no option and the *past* notice ("el 1 de junio" on 15 June). "Del año que viene" ("de l'any que ve", "next year") puts the month in the coming year: "el 20 de julio del año que viene" is 20 July 2027, beyond the horizon. Said with a month before a day ("el año que viene en enero el sábado 9", "en enero del año que viene el sábado 16") or before a colon ("next January: Saturday the 9th or Saturday the 16th"), the month frames the days that follow (owner, 2026-11-13).
rules.R5: A bare weekday, "este", "el próximo" and "que viene" all mean the first coming one; today is never the answer. A bare weekday added with "y también" ("i també", "and also") to a week already named in the phrase, or to a stretch inside one week, belongs to that week ("cualquier tarde de la semana que viene excepto el jueves, y también el sábado" = Saturday 27; "del 6 al 10 de julio y también el sábado" = Saturday 11 July; owner, 2026-11-12). A week named after several weekdays holds every one of them ("el martes o el miércoles de la semana que viene" = 23 and 24 June, never tomorrow; "que vienen" after them is "que viene"; owner, 2026-11-12). A bare weekday joined by "o" ("o si no", "or failing that") right after a dated day is the first one after that date: "el viernes 26 o el sábado" = 26 and 27 June, "el 10 de julio o el sábado" = 10 and 11 July, while "el sábado o el viernes 26" is still 20 and 26 June (owner, 2026-11-12). The Catalan weekday abbreviations dl, dt (dm), dc, dj, dv, ds and dg are weekdays where a weekday can stand: joined to another weekday ("dm o dc de la setmana que ve" = 23 and 24 June, "del dl al dv de la setmana que ve" = 22→26 June) or followed by its day, time or week ("dg a les 6", "dt 23 de juny"); elsewhere they are ordinary words ("música con dj el sábado", "DJ and drinks"; owner, 2026-11-12). A week said right before weekdays ("next week, Wednesday or Thursday at 8 pm", "la semana que viene el martes", "la setmana que ve, dimecres o dijous") is the week they belong to: 24 and 25 June, never a week of options plus this week's days; one joined to the week by "y" or "o" is not framed (owner, 2026-11-13). A chat "x" is Wednesday where a weekday can stand ("el x a las 20:00"); before "la tarde", "la noche", "la tarda", "la nit" it is "por"/"per" ("el vie x la noche a las 9 y media" = Friday 21:30), and at the end of a message it is nothing ("Friday at 8pm x"; owner, 2026-11-13).
rules.R6: "Este finde", "el próximo fin de semana" and "el finde que viene" all mean the first coming weekend.
rules.R7: A bare day number means its next occurrence ("el día 10" on 15 June: 10 July); the number of today itself gives no option and the *unclear* notice.
rules.R9: A vague time ("por la tarde", "por la noche") keeps the date, a whole day or a range, with no time, and is reported with a notice of its own, *timeUnclear* (the day is marked, the time was not understood and is picked in the next step). An hour that does not exist said of a date is reported the same way and never read as a day ("el viernes a las 25" = Friday, whole day). A vague time between the weekdays and their period keeps the days ("los sábados por la noche de julio"). In English the half of the day said after the hour is its mark, not a vague time ("10 at night on Friday" = Friday 22:00). When something else in the phrase is not understood either, the notice is the general *unclear*. "Cualquier tarde de la semana del 6 de julio", "any evening …" is a vague time over those days, one single-day option each (R16 when one is left out); so is Catalan "a quarts de deu", which says no exact hour. "Todo el día" and "all day" are the whole day, with no time and no notice (owner, 2026-11-12). "After work" is a vague afternoon as "por la tarde" is, and a lunch word such as "a la hora de comer", "a l'hora de dinar" or "lunchtime" with no hour is a vague time too, never 14:00: "Thursday after work" = Thursday, the time reported, "Thursday after work, like 6-ish" = Thursday 18:00, "el domingo a la hora de comer" = Sunday, the time reported (owner, 2026-11-12). "Cualquier día" over a stretch with a day left out is one single-day option per day, as "cualquier tarde" is: "cualquier día del 13 al 31 de julio menos el 25" = 13–24 and 26–31 July, one by one (owner, 2026-11-12). "Entre semana", "laborable", "weekday", "entre setmana" after "cualquier"/"any" ("cualquier día laborable de la semana del 6 al 10 de julio", "any weekday evening in the week of 20 July") or after a stretch ("la semana que viene entre semana") keep Monday to Friday of it, one single-day option each (owner, 2026-11-13). "Cualquier día" right after a stretch is each day of it: "de hoy hasta el viernes cualquier día a partir de las seis de la tarde" = 15–19 June at 18:00, nothing reported (owner, 2026-11-13). Plural "las mañanas", "les matinades" is the part of the day, never "mañana" (tomorrow), and a morning from an hour to an earlier one runs past noon: "las mañanas del 22 al 26 de 10 a 1" = 22–26 June 10:00–13:00, while "mañana por la mañana" is still tomorrow morning (owner, 2026-11-13).
rules.R10: "A mediodía" is 12:00; "a partir de las 19" is 19:00. "Las" (Catalan "les") before a number is an hour, never a day of the month, also with no "a" before it ("sábado de las 22", "sábado las 22", "a las 10 y las 12"; owner, 2026-11-12); after a weekday, so is "de" before a number ("sábado de 22" = 22:00), and English "from" before an hour is "desde". "Sobre las 11", "a las 11 o así" and "8ish" are the hour as said (owner, 2026-11-12); so are Catalan "cap a les 21", "aproximadamente", "y algo" ("las 2 y algo de la madrugada" = 02:00) and English "around" inside a range ("from 10 pm to around 3 am"). English "from … to …" with hours ("July 4 from noon to 6pm" = 12:00–18:00, "6 to 9 pm" = 18:00–21:00) is "de … a …", and "after 6 pm" or "from 2" is "a partir de" (owner, 2026-11-12). English "around" before several hours reaches all of them ("tomorrow at around 8 or 9" = two hours tomorrow, never 9 July; owner, 2026-11-12). "Y pico" is "y algo" and "like 6-ish", "como a las" and Catalan "més o menys" are the hour as said: "el viernes a las 2 y pico" = 02:00 or 14:00, "dissabte a les 8 més o menys" = 08:00 or 20:00 (owner, 2026-11-12). "Anytime after 8" is "after 8", and a part of the day said before it settles its half: "Thursday or Friday evening, anytime after 8" = 20:00 both days; so is "a cualquier hora a partir de las 6" (owner, 2026-11-13).
rules.R11: A time that is not a quarter hour is moved back to the quarter it falls in ("20:10" = 20:00, "8:29" = 08:15, "8:59" = 08:45).
rules.R12: A time on a range or a weekend gives one single-day option per day, each with the time.
rules.R13: One time after several days joined by "o"/"y" applies to all of them; so does a time said before them ("a las 8 el viernes o el sábado"), for the days that have no time of their own. The same hour said again with "también" ("i també", "too") takes the part of the day said for it once ("hoy a las 10 de la noche o mañana a las 10 también" = 22:00 both days; "el sábado a las 10 y el domingo también a las 10 de la mañana" = 10:00 both days; owner, 2026-11-12). "A la misma hora", "a esa misma hora", "same time", "a la mateixa hora" is the last hour said in the phrase, its half of the day still asked when not said: "pasado mañana a las 21:00 o el viernes a la misma hora" = 21:00 both days; with no hour said before it is reported (owner, 2026-11-13). "Siempre", "sempre", "todos", "both days", "either day" next to a time after several days say that time is each day's and are not reported: "el lunes 22 y el martes 23 o bien el jueves 25, siempre por la tarde" = the three days, the time reported (owner, 2026-11-13).
rules.R14: Days listed one by one are separate options, even when consecutive; "los días" before them is ignored ("los días 3, 4 y 5 de julio"; owner, 2026-11-12).
rules.R15: "La semana que viene" and "la semana del 6" give one range, Monday to Sunday; "la semana del 12 de agosto" is the week containing that date, whatever its weekday.
rules.R16: A range with one day excluded splits into the ranges left; a lone day left is a single option. English "except" inside a range is "menos" ("from July 6 to July 10 except July 8" = 6→7 and 9→10 July). A vague time over a week or a stretch with a day excluded ("cualquier tarde de la semana que viene excepto el jueves") gives the days left one by one, each a single-day option, with the vague time reported (R9); another day added after it ("y también el sábado por la mañana") is added as R9 says (owner, 2026-11-12). English ordinal words are days of the month, "sixth" to "thirty-first" as "first" to "fifth", and one after "except" said of a stretch of days is a day: "from the sixth through the tenth of july except the eighth" = 6→7 and 9→10 July (owner, 2026-11-12). A vague time said after the exception is the whole phrase's, never the exception's, so the day is still left out and the time reported (R9): "toda la semana que viene menos el miércoles por la noche" = 22→23 and 25→28 June (owner, 2026-11-12). After an exception, ", y …" (", i …", ", and …") goes on with the phrase, a day added as with "y también" (R5): "qualsevol nit de la setmana del 22 menys dijous, i el dissabte al matí també" = 22–24 and 26–28 June, one by one (owner, 2026-11-12). An English ordinal in words listed after a day of the month is a day too: "the twenty first of august or the twenty second" = 21 and 22 August (owner, 2026-11-13).
rules.R17: Fixed-date holidays are understood; movable ones (Semana Santa, a "puente") are not, for now, nor what is named by one ("Easter weekend", "el puente de mayo"). A fixed holiday followed by "que es" ("que és", "which is") and a date only names that date, which is the one read: "la revetlla de Sant Joan, que és dimarts 23, des de les 10 de la nit …" = Tuesday 23 June from 22:00 (owner, 2026-11-12). A holiday adds its date only when the phrase gives no date of its own; beside one it names the plan: "los sábados 5, 12 y 19 de diciembre para la cena de navidad" adds no 25 December, while "la cena de navidad" alone is 25 December (one listed with the dates by "y", "o" or a comma is still one of them: "Nochebuena o el 26 de diciembre"). A vague time word right after a word no rule reads names the plan too ("game night", "quiz night") and gives way to the hour said: "game night 6/27 or 7/11 8pm" = 20:00 both days; with no hour said it is a vague time ("quiz night on Friday" = Friday, the time reported; owner, 2026-11-12). A movable holiday beside a date of the phrase's own names the plan, as a fixed one does: "el puente de diciembre del 5 al 8 de diciembre" = 5→8 December, nothing reported (owner, 2026-11-13). "La revetlla de Sant Joan", "la verbena de San Juan", "la nit de Sant Joan" and "la noche de San Juan" are 23 June, the eve, and beside their own date they name the plan: "la revetlla de st joan, el 23 a partir de les 10 de la nit" = 23 June 22:00 (owner, 2026-11-13). "Next" or "this" beside a fixed holiday ("el próximo día de Sant Joan", "el San Juan que viene", "esta Navidad", "next Christmas") is the coming one, as the holiday alone; said on the holiday itself, "this" is today and "next" is next year's ("el próximo San Juan" said on 24 June 2026 = 24 June 2027; owner, 2026-11-13).
rules.R18: "Antes del 20" and "hasta" count from today; the limit day of "hasta" is included, the one of "antes de" is not. Without a weekday ("antes del 19", "de aquí al jueves") they give one single-day option per day.
rules.R19: Past, impossible or out-of-horizon dates give no option, each with its notice: *past*, *mismatch* ("el 31 de junio" does not exist; a day and month are looked for in this year and the next, so "29 de febrero" does not exist when neither has it), *horizon* (beyond 12 months). When only part of what a fragment asks for lies beyond the 12 months, the part within is kept and the *horizon* notice names the fragment ("todos los lunes de junio de 2027" on 15 June 2026: 7 and 14 June; "los próximos 4294967296 fines de semana": the 52 that fit); a range of days that crosses the limit is cut at it ("del 10 al 20 de junio de 2027": 10 to 15 June). No number makes the reader fail: "dentro de 4294967296 días" is beyond the 12 months, and a year in figures outside 2000–2100 is read as the nearest of them, which is past or beyond the 12 months all the same ("20/7/1999", "todos los lunes del 1/7/2026 al 31/12/9998": the Mondays within the 12 months). A range written backwards gives *mismatch* ("del 20 de agosto de 2026 al 10 de agosto de 2026"), and so does a count of zero ("los próximos 0 lunes"); a month of a past year and the days before today give *past* ("julio de 2025", "todos los lunes de julio de 2025", "antes del 15 de junio" on 15 June) (owner, 2026-11-14).
rules.R20: "Todos los días de julio" gives one option per day; above 60 options nothing is proposed, with the *tooMany* notice.
rules.R21: "Dentro de dos semanas" is the day 14 days from today. "A fortnight on Saturday" is the coming Saturday plus 14 days (4 July; owner, 2026-11-13).
rules.R22: A bare month ("en agosto", "el mes que viene") is one range, first to last day. Months said from one to another ("de julio a septiembre", "entre julio y septiembre", "desde julio hasta septiembre") are every month between them, as when they are listed, for a pattern or an ordinal weekday; alone they are one range, from the first day of one to the last of the other (owner, 2026-11-12), and what is left of it when already started (R31). A month said only after the last day of a range of days is the month of both ends: "entre el 1 y el 15 de septiembre" = 1→15 September, "todos los días entre el 28 y el 3 de agosto" = 28 July → 3 August (owner, 2026-11-13).
rules.R23: "La primera quincena de julio" is one range, 1 to 15; a vague part of a month alone ("a mediados de julio") gives no option and the *unclear* notice.
rules.R24: A weekday that contradicts its date ("el martes 3 de julio" when the 3rd is a Friday) gives no option and the *does not fit* notice. A month written after the last of several days joined by "o"/"y" is for the earlier days too, and an earlier day whose weekday does not fit that month but fits the month before is in the month before: "el lunes 29 o el miércoles 1 de julio" = 29 June and 1 July, while "el martes 29 o el miércoles 1 de julio" keeps the *does not fit* notice for the 29th (owner, 2026-11-12). A weekday after "que es", "o sea", "es decir", "és a dir", "i.e." names the day already said just before it, never a new one: "el 7 de julio a las 21:30, que es martes" = 7 July 21:30 only, "el divendres 26 per la nit, o sea el viernes, a les 10" = 26 June 22:00; one that does not fit that day gives no option and the *does not fit* notice ("el 7 de julio, que es lunes"; owner, 2026-11-13). A month said before a colon is the month of what follows: "dic: los sábados 5, 12 y 19" = 5, 12 and 19 December, "octubre: todos los sábados por la tarde" = the Saturdays of October (owner, 2026-11-13). "Los dos", "els dos", "tots dos", "both" after options is an aside, never day 2, and a bare weekday set right after dated days says which weekday they are, never a new day: "el 3 o el 10 de julio, viernes los dos, a las 8 de la tarde" = 3 and 10 July 20:00, "el 3 de julio, viernes" = 3 July; one that does not fit gives no option and the *does not fit* notice ("el 3 o el 10 de julio, sábado los dos"); one joined by "o" is still an option (R5; owner, 2026-11-13).
rules.R25: "The one after the next" week or weekend is the second coming one. "El siguiente sábado o domingo" ("the following Saturday or Sunday", "el següent dissabte o diumenge") said as an option after a named weekend is that weekend's Saturday or Sunday a week later: "este finde, o si no el siguiente sábado o domingo" = 20→21 June, 27 June and 28 June; alone, "el siguiente sábado" is the coming one (R5; owner, 2026-11-13).
rules.R26: A weekend belongs to the month its Saturday falls in; "los dos primeros fines de semana de julio" gives that many ranges. "Cualquier fin de semana de septiembre", "any weekend in <month>", "qualsevol cap de setmana de <mes>" are the weekends of that month, one range each, minus the ones left out: "any weekend in September except the 12th and 13th" = 5→6, 19→20 and 26→27 September, "any weekend in july except the first one" = the last three (owner, 2026-11-13).
rules.R27: A condition unrelated to dates ("si arreglan el coche") is ignored and not reported. So is an aside that says nothing about dates: "tonight at 7 or 8, your call" = 19:00 and 20:00 today (owner, 2026-11-12). A word that speaks of dates is never ignored as part of a condition: "y si no pasado" after "mañana" is "pasado mañana" ("mañana a las nueve de la noche y si no pasado a las nueve también" = 16 and 17 June at 21:00), and one that no rule reads is reported ("el viernes a las 8 de la tarde y si no pasado" reports "pasado"; owner, 2026-11-12). The words after "para", "pa", "per", "for" that hold no date word (no number, weekday, month, time or date word) name the plan and are not reported: "el domingo 28 de junio de 12:00 a 15:00 para el vermut" = 28 June 12:00–15:00, while "para el sábado" is still Saturday; every other left-over is still reported ("…, cena en casa de Marta" reports "casa de Marta"). "As usual" and "whichever suits" are asides, and a game's number is its name: "5 a side Tuesday and Wednesday at 7pm", "fútbol 7 el sábado" (owner, 2026-11-13).
rules.R28: A bare hour from 1 to 11 with nothing saying morning or afternoon is never guessed: the option carries both readings ("a las 5" = 05:00 or 17:00, shown as `05:00?17:00`) and the app asks "¿mañana o tarde?", one question per distinct time; a range is one question ("de 5 a 7"), and "de 10 a 2" can only be 10:00–14:00. No question for 12 (noon), 13–23, "de la tarde", "pm", "09:00" or a breakfast or dinner word ("cena a las 9" = 21:00); a lunch word says afternoon for 12 to 4 ("comida a las 2" = 14:00), a "merienda" word for 4 to 8; "almuerzo" and any other word leave the hour asked. The half of the day said in words next to a date ("por la tarde", "viernes tarde", "sábado mañana") is for that date's times only, never for another day's ("el viernes a las 8 y el sábado por la tarde" asks Friday's hour and reports Saturday's vague time, R9; a meal word still speaks for the whole phrase): said before a time, it is for that time and the ones listed after it ("por la tarde a las 5 o a las 6"; said before the date too, "por la tarde, el viernes a las 8"); said after times, in words or with the last clock ("a las 8 o a las 9 por la tarde", "at 8 or 9 pm"), it is for the ones before it that have none and are no later hour ("a las 10 o a las 5 de la tarde" asks the 10); a time after it is asked ("a las 8 de la tarde o a las 9"). English "half past eight" is 8:30 and "quarter to nine" 8:45; Catalan quarters count toward the next hour ("un quart de deu" = 9:15, "dos quarts de deu" = 9:30, "dos quarts d'onze" = 10:30, "tres quarts de deu" = 9:45); their half of the day is asked when not said ("pm", "del vespre" and "del matí" settle it; owner, 2026-11-12). British "half eight" is 8:30, its half of the day asked when not said: "next Friday at half eight PM" = Friday 20:30, "on Saturday at half seven" = 07:30 or 19:30 (owner, 2026-11-12). A meal word settles the half of the day of a bare hour but never invents one: "a la hora de comer", "a l'hora de dinar" and "(around) lunchtime" are lunch words ("Friday the 26th around lunchtime, say 1ish" = 26 June 13:00), and "temprano" or "early" between the half of the day and the hour does not keep them apart ("el domingo por la mañana temprano, como a las 9 o 9 y algo" = Sunday 09:00, one option; owner, 2026-11-12). "Noche de …" (also "la noche de San Juan"), "después de currar", "después del trabajo", "després de la feina" and "after work" settle the half of the day of a bare hour ("jueves 18 o viernes 19 después de currar, sobre las 7" = 19:00 both days, "noche de pelis el viernes a las 10" = 22:00); "al migdia", "al mediodía" right beside a bare hour from 1 to 4 is a lunch word ("dissabte a la 1 al migdia" = 13:00, "el domingo al mediodía, a las 2" = 14:00), and alone it is 12:00 (R10; owner, 2026-11-13).
rules.R29: Midnight said of a day as a single time is 00:00 of the next day ("el viernes a medianoche", "a las 12 de la noche" and "a las 24:00" = Saturday 00:00; "a las 00:00" stays 00:00 of the day named). A time range can cross midnight: it stays one option on the day it starts, with its end on the next day (`nextDay: true`, shown "(+1)"), up to 06:00: "el viernes de 22 a 2" = Friday 22:00 > 02:00 (+1); one that ends at midnight ends at 00:00 (+1) ("el viernes de 10 a 12 de la noche" = Friday 22:00 > 00:00 (+1)); one that ends later than 06:00 is not accepted: the day is kept with no time and the range is reported with a notice of its own, *tooLate* ("el viernes de 22 a 8" = Friday, whole day; in "el viernes de 22 a 8 y el sábado de 20 a 23" Saturday keeps its time). A range that starts at midnight said of a day falls on the next day ("el sábado de medianoche a 2" = Sunday 00:00–02:00; "la noche del viernes de las 12 a las 3 de la madrugada" = Saturday 00:00–03:00). Catalan "de la matinada" is "de la madrugada" (owner, 2026-11-12). Midnight with no day gives no option. Each time block is its own option; blocks that overlap on the same date are kept apart, never merged, and only an exact duplicate is dropped. Midnight at the end of the last day of the 12 months is beyond them: "el 15 de junio de 2027 a medianoche" on 15 June 2026 gives no option and *horizon*; a range of that day that ends after midnight is kept (owner, 2026-11-14).
rules.R31: A date range already started gives what is left of it, from today ("del 10 al 20 de junio" on 15 June: 15 to 20); one already finished follows R4. A weekday pattern over a range of days is read over the same days as the range said alone: "todos los lunes del 10 al 20 de junio" on 15 June is the 15th; a range under way gives what is left of it with its year written too ("del 10 al 20 de junio de 2026" on 17 June: 17 to 20); "todos los jueves del 3 al 7 de junio" gives *past*; a weekday that contradicts its date gives *mismatch* (R24) (owner, 2026-11-14).
rules.R32: Two weekdays with the week they belong to ("del lunes al jueves de la semana que viene") are a range inside that week; of a week already started, what is left of it (owner confirmed, 2026-11-11).
rules.R33: Several ordinals before one weekday or one weekend give one option each: "el primero y el segundo lunes de diciembre", "el primer, el segundo y el último lunes de agosto", "el primer y el tercer lunes de cada mes hasta septiembre", "el primer o el segundo finde de julio"; also written with figures ("el 1er y el 3er lunes", "the 1st and 3rd Monday"), "penúltimo", and counted ("los dos primeros lunes de julio", "the last two Fridays of August"). A month said once serves the ordinal weekdays before it ("el primer lunes y el segundo martes de julio"). Several months give the ordinal in each ("el primer lunes de julio y de agosto", "de cada mes de julio a septiembre"), a year after the month is read ("de marzo de 2027"), and a weekend is also counted in this month or the next ("el último finde del mes", "el primer finde del mes que viene"). When some of them are already past, what is left is given, as with a range already started with no notice (owner, 2026-11-12).
rules.R34: A date written with figures and a slash is day/month ("7/4" = 7 April); when the organizer's browser region is the United States ("en-US", "es-US") it is month/day ("7/4" = 4 July). When one order cannot be a date, the other is read, whatever the region ("7/14" and "14/7" = 14 July). The editor never reorders the figures (owner, 2026-11-12).
rules.R30: Not understood by decision: rejecting one occurrence and pointing to the following one (*unclear*); numbers that are not dates and no date, or nothing about when at all ("hola, qué tal"), are *does not fit*; a phrase that speaks of when without saying it ("cuando haga bueno") is *unclear*, and so is one that corrects itself when the rules read it alone ("el sábado a las 10, no, a las 11"; owner, 2026-11-12); such a phrase is sent to the editor, which keeps only the correction, and that reading is the right one: "el sábado a las 10, no, a las 11" = Saturday 11:00 or 23:00 (owner, 2026-11-13). A number that is not a date beside dates is ignored ("Os propongo tres opciones: el martes 23 de junio a las 20:30, …" reads the three dates; owner, 2026-11-12).
